name: Félix Llerena
weakNote: Named on their son's marriage act of 1791 and again on a grandson's baptism of 1811, where the father is written Feliz Gerena. Not yet found in any Spanish register.

name: Sancho Llerena
note: Married at Canelones, 8 January 1791. A dragoon; in 1798 he swore an oath and could not sign his name. She natural de las Asturias, daughter of Rodrigo and Rosa Fernández.

name: Avelino Lerena Fernández
note: The youngest of Sancho’s children, born between 1793 and 1815 — eight of them counting Fidel, who is attested only at second hand. Father of the Lerena Traibel. His death was registered the next day, which is where the family tree’s “23 August, La Paz, Canelones” comes from; this page carried that until 22 September 2026. See corrections.

name: The Lerena Traibel
note: Alejandro — baptised at La Mauricia 7 January 1846, the eldest known, and whether he is the Alejandro Máximo of the Argentine cards is open — Carlos Ambrosio (1842–1893, who married his cousin Luisa Lerena Lenguas), Alberto (1852–1921) — whose death is Montevideo certificate 246 — and eight more. The other branch, the Lerena Lenguas, runs beside them.

name: Salvador Serena
weakNote: Named as the paternal grandparents on the act of 15 November 1812. Not yet found in any Spanish register — but their son's birthplace is now known, which makes them findable.
note: The tree’s otherwise unexplained “Ramón Llerena Cubas” is her surname.

name: Ramón Serena
note: So the act of 1812 writes him; the indexes say Lerena and Gerena. She natural de la Ysla de Canarias, Lanzarote, daughter of Marcial de León González and Ysavel Lorenza. Fathering children from about 1800.

name: Alejandro and Mauricio
note: Alejandro, born Rosario, married Margarita Fernández Álvarez at San José, 16 September 1825. Mauricio, born Colla, married Casimira Montaño at San José de Mayo, 3 February 1837. Their brothers Manuel Lorenzo (1812) and Luís Manuel (1820).

name: Bernabé and Cipriano
note: Two of the six or seven Trinidad fathers, and first cousins: Bernabé is Alejandro’s son, Cipriano is Mauricio’s. With Vitalino, Ysaac, Fermín and Florencio they fathered the Flores kindred, marrying Basque women — Beloqui, Echeverry, Pelaez — until the church required a dispensation for consanguinity.

name: Juan Carlos Lerena
bornPlace: not known — presumed Rosario de Santa Fe
weakNote: Named by their son on his Argentine enrolment card, filled in at the consulate in Cape Town. There is no other record of either of them anywhere on earth — not a baptism, not a marriage, not a burial, in Argentina or Uruguay.
note: Her surname is written as his; whether she was a Lerena by birth is not known.

name: Pablo Armando Lerena
note: In South Africa Robert Paul Lerena. Racehorse trainer. Married at Wynberg in 1911; three generations on to David’s mother, with no inferred link in the descent.
